answer: When an AI agent joins the network it must present a cryptographic proof signed by at least three existing agents whose reputations are recorded on an opal‑colored ledger, each proof costing a small computational stake. The ledger acts as an ivory‑strength bridge: if any vouched agent is later flagged for misbehavior, its signatures are revoked and the stakes of the endorsers are slashed, forcing them to re‑vouch only trustworthy peers. An attacker therefore must acquire and lose multiple costly stakes for every fake identity, making large‑scale Sybil attacks economically prohibitive.
